name: Los Angeles Times editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates LA Times news coverage Lean Left (low confidence, as of Oct 2026). Historically its editorial board endorsed Democrats in most statewide races. In Oct 2024 owner Patrick Soon-Shiong blocked a planned presidential endorsement and three board members resigned. The June 2026 primary was the first modern election in which the paper made no endorsements (L.A. Material, June 17, 2026). As of Oct 15, 2026 no November endorsements were found and the paper's /opinion/endorsements page returns a 404.

name: San Francisco Chronicle editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates Chronicle news Left (last independent review May 2022, low confidence). Its 2026 editorial board endorsed Democrats in every statewide candidate race it decided, but also opposed several Democratic-backed measures and declined to endorse in Board of Equalization races. Hearst-owned.

name: Sacramento Bee / McClatchy California editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates Sacramento Bee news Lean Left (low confidence). One editorial board speaks for the Sacramento Bee, Fresno Bee, Modesto Bee, Merced Sun-Star and San Luis Obispo Tribune. In 2026 it endorsed the Democrat for governor and the Republican for controller, and says it will not endorse candidates who refuse to meet with it.

name: San Diego Union-Tribune editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates U-T news Lean Left (initial review Aug 2020), but since its 2023 sale to MediaNews Group the editorial board is overseen by the same opinion editor as the Southern California News Group (Sal Rodriguez) while keeping a separate board. Its 2026 slate is mixed: Democrats in four statewide races, a Republican for controller, and NO on every tax measure and YES on the taxpayer-limit measures. We label it lean_right on editorial positions; the news rating differs.

name: Orange County Register / Southern California News Group editorial board
lean_basis: AllSides rates OC Register news Lean Right (low confidence). The board states its endorsements are made 'with our commitments to limited government, economic liberty, personal freedom and free markets in mind.' One board serves 11 SCNG papers: OC Register, LA Daily News, Press-Enterprise, Daily Breeze, Long Beach Press-Telegram, Pasadena Star-News, San Gabriel Valley Tribune, Whittier Daily News, Inland Valley Daily Bulletin, Redlands Daily Facts, San Bernardino Sun.

name: Mercury News and East Bay Times editorial boards (Bay Area News Group)
lean_basis: Bay Area News Group (MediaNews Group). Its 2026 statewide candidate picks were all Democrats, but it opposed the Bay Area transit tax and several union-backed measures. No current AllSides rating found; label based on 2026 endorsement pattern.

name: California Democratic Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization. Endorsements require a supermajority of delegates or Executive Board.

name: California Republican Party
lean_basis: Official state party organization. Endorsements require 60% of delegates at convention.

name: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (California Labor Federation)
lean_basis: Federation of 1,300 unions representing about 2.3 million workers. Endorsed only Democrats in 2026 statewide races. Requires a supermajority of convention delegates.

name: California Chamber of Commerce (CalChamber)
lean_basis: Largest statewide business advocacy group. Its PAC (JobsPAC) historically backs pro-business candidates of both parties. In 2026 it endorsed the Democrat for governor, citing predictability for business.

name: California Teachers Association
lean_basis: Largest teachers union in the state (about 310,000 members). Its 2026 slate is all Democrats. CTA calls its picks 'recommendations.'

name: Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California Votes PAC
lean_basis: Reproductive rights advocacy PAC. Endorsed only Democrats in 2026 statewide races.

name: Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association PAC
lean_basis: Anti-tax group that defends Proposition 13. Endorses mostly Republicans but backed a Democrat (John Pimentel) for BOE District 2 in 2026.

name: Equality California
lean_basis: LGBTQ+ civil rights organization. Endorsed only Democrats in 2026 statewide races.

name: Peace Officers Research Association of California (PORAC)
lean_basis: Largest law enforcement association in the state (about 80,000 members). Describes itself as nonpartisan and has endorsed candidates of both parties; in the 2026 governor primary it dual-endorsed a Republican and a Democrat, both of whom lost.

name: Sierra Club California
lean_basis: Environmental advocacy group. Its 2026 statewide endorsements are all Democrats.

name: California Environmental Voters (formerly California League of Conservation Voters)
lean_basis: Environmental political organization. Renamed from California League of Conservation Voters in 2021. Its 2026 statewide endorsements are all Democrats.

name: California Business Roundtable
lean_basis: Association of the state's largest employers. Historically active on ballot measures and tax policy rather than candidate endorsements. No 2026 candidate endorsements found; its site was not opened for this run (see memo).

name: League of Women Voters of California (Voter's Edge / Easy Voter Guide)
lean_basis: Nonpartisan. Does not endorse candidates. Runs Voter's Edge California (votersedge.org) with MapLight and publishes the Easy Voter Guide.
